info.bio:
Grace Jones (19 de mayo de 1948), nacida Grace Mendoza en Spanish Town (Kingston, Jamaica) es una modelo, cantante y actriz.

Jones destaca por su sofisticada imagen y una apariencia perturbadoramente andrógina que a finales de los 70 y principios de los 80 cuestionaba agresivamente tanto los estereotipos raciales como los sexuales y de género asociados al cuerpo de una mujer negra.

Grace Mendoza nació el 19 de mayo de 1948 en Spanishtown (Jamaica).

scenes.name: Postdisco, electro y el reinado del DJ
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Tras la saturación de Fiebre del sábado noche, la disco vuelve al underground gay negro e hispano (Paradise Garage, Larry Levan): sellos como West End, Prelude y Sleeping Bag, cajas de ritmos, bajos sintetizados y reverb dub, remixes de Walter Gibbons, Shep Pettibone y François Kevorkian, el electro derivado de Kraftwerk y el freestyle latino. Arthur Russell, vanguardista gay e hippie, ve en la disco el minimalismo de Riley y Reich (Dinosaur L, «Go Bang!»). Grace Jones, con Sly and Robbie en Compass Point, versiona a The Normal, Joy Division y The Pretenders (Warm Leatherette, Nightclubbing). New Order y A Certain Ratio absorben esta Nueva York y la llevan a Manchester con The Haçienda.
scenes.family: Ritmos negros: dub, funk, disco y hip hop

scenes.name: ZTT: Art of Noise y Propaganda
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: El sello de Trevor Horn y su esposa Jill Sinclair, con Paul Morley, harto del periodismo, como director artístico, redactor de manifiestos y saqueador del futurismo (el nombre viene de Marinetti vía Russolo): series «Acción» e «Incidental», guerra al new pop descarriado. Art of Noise (Anne Dudley, J. J. Jeczalik, Gary Langan) nace del aburrimiento durante la grabación de 90125 de Yes, metiendo un break de batería entero en el Fairlight: Into Battle with the Art of Noise, «Beat Box», «Moments in Love», «Close (to the Edit)». Anónimos, con llaves inglesas en lugar de fotos: hip hop como si se hubiera inventado en Europa en 1916, entre Dada y el futuro big beat. Propaganda, de Düsseldorf, eurodisco épico de los «hijos de Fritz Lang y Giorgio Moroder» (A Secret Wish, «Duel»). La marca acaba comiéndose el producto y los artistas huyen de sus contratos leoninos.

scenes.name: Música disco
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El funk abre la puerta a la subcultura disco: los gays de Nueva York, perseguidos, crean sus islas sociales en clubes privados y recuperan la despersonalización del éxtasis colectivo. Tres hechos la impulsan: el soul orquestal de Barry White, «Autobahn» de Kraftwerk y el Polymoog. Manu Dibango («Soul Makossa») y MFSB la inventan; Giorgio Moroder casa la música robótica de Kraftwerk con el soul (Donna Summer, «I Feel Love», nacimiento del synth-pop). Van McCoy, el maxi de 12" de Walter Gibbons, Chic, Grace Jones, Gloria Gaynor, Saturday Night Fever, el Warehouse de Frankie Knuckles y el Paradise Garage de Larry Levan. Los reyes del pop: Michael Jackson (Thriller, «el mayor farol de todos los tiempos») y Prince, su contrapartida intelectual.
scenes.family: Soul, funk, disco, hip hop y baile

scenes.name: Pop de club de los ochenta
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: La disco sale del gueto: apogeo de los extended mixes y del DJ remezclador (John Morales, Shep Pettibone, Jellybean, Kevorkian) que convierte cualquier estilo en dance hit. Grace Jones, Madonna —surgida de las discotecas con Jellybean y Nile Rodgers— y Prince, «la gran fuerza creadora de los ochenta», un artista electrónico para los músicos de Detroit.

podcast.title: Parisian Fashion Icon (1970-1976)
podcast.body: After being discovered by a European modeling representative, Grace Jones moved to Paris, where her unique physique was embraced by the city's radical and artistic fashion scene. She quickly became an icon, modeling for major haute couture houses of the 1970s, including Yves Saint Laurent, Kenzo, and Balmain. "se la lleva a parís y en prácticamente nada gresios se convierte en todo un icono de la ciudad."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Androgynous Tuxedo Look (1976)
podcast.body: In 1976, Grace Jones made history on the runway by appearing in a man's tuxedo for Yves Saint Laurent's collection. While initially regarded by some fashion critics as one of the most "unpleasant" images of the Paris runway, this look rapidly became an iconic moment in fashion history within two to three years. "ella pasaría la historia de la moda cuando en mil novecientos sesventa y seis en la colección de Issa Nuran salía a vestir a con esmoquim de obra de esfilar."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Island Records Contract (Late 1976)
podcast.body: Grace Jones signed her first record deal with Island Records in late 1976. This contract was initially a speculative venture, as she was a model transitioning into music, seeking to remain active in the entertainment industry. "fue muy poco después de llegar a finales de 1976 cuando ya firmó ese contrato a mislan recos fue realmente un contrato un poco a ver qué pasaba porque ella realmente era una modelo que venía a reconvertirse en algo un poco pues para seguir en activo."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: "Queen of Gay Discos" and Anti-Disco Backlash (1979)
podcast.body: At the peak of her success in 1979, coinciding with the release of a work described as "Queen of Gay Discos," Grace Jones's popularity was negatively impacted by the anti-disco riots. During this period, conservative groups publicly burned disco albums, leading to widespread censorship in many conservative parts of the United States. "cuando saca el mío y de Queen of Gay Discos pues lamentablemente bien el problema porque justo en 1979 se generan los estúrbios antidiscos."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Reinvention After Anti-Disco Riots (1979)
podcast.body: While the anti-disco riots of 1979 signaled the end for many disco artists, for Grace Jones, it was merely another step in her career and a crucial moment for reinterpretation, ultimately propelling her to even greater heights. She is characterized as a figure of constant reinvention, relentless provocation, and always pushing boundaries. "para grillos no solo fue un paso más en su carrera sino que fue el momento de una reinterpretación que la gría incluso volver todavía más alto porque ella es un personaje de reinvención constante de provocación constante y de siempre ir más allá."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: "New Gloria Gaynor" of Electronic Disco
podcast.body: During a period of crisis for the disco movement, Grace Jones quickly established herself as the "new Gloria Gaynor." She championed a more electronic and, at times, "gay" version of disco, which rapidly gained popularity in the late 1970s and early 1980s, coinciding with the rise of groups like Village People. "ella prácticamente en cuanto sale se alza como la nueva Gloria Gaynor de ese nuevo disco más electrónico un tanto a veces gay que se hizo tan popular ya final de los 70 y tirando a los primeros años de los 80."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Dynamic Personality and Image
podcast.body: Grace Jones, a Jamaican model, singer, record producer, songwriter, and actress, possessed a personality and image so versatile that she felt at home in any club across the world, regardless of the dance music genre played. Her unique presence allowed her to transcend musical boundaries. "Her personality and image was such that she was at home at any kind of club anywhere in the world that played any kind of dance music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 4: Alt-Dance

podcast.title: Early 1980s Dance Club Music
podcast.body: In the early 1980s, Grace Jones produced music that was described as cool, slinky, and sufficiently outside the mainstream to appeal to the alternative crowd in their non-disco dance clubs, particularly in the UK. Her sound helped bridge the gap between various dance genres. "And here's the kind of stuff she was making for dance clubs in the early 1980s. Cool, slinky, and just outside of the mainstream enough to work with the alternative crowd in their non-disco dance clubs, especially in the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 4: Alt-Dance

podcast.title: Early Modeling Career in US (Late 1960s/Early 1970s)
podcast.body: Born in Jamaica, Grace Jones moved to the United States at a young age and began modeling while still a student in the late 1960s and early 1970s. However, her distinctive physical appearance did not find much success in the then-conservative American fashion scene. "no tiene mucho éxito en Estados Unidos estamos hablando de finales el los 60 primer año de los 70 donde pues en Estados Unidos aún había una versión bastante conservadora de la moda entonces digamos que el físico de gresios no tuvo mucho éxito."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: End of Parisian Modeling Career (Age 28)
podcast.body: Grace Jones concluded her modeling career in Paris at the age of 28, a relatively advanced age for models in an industry that favored youth and radicalism. Following this, she returned to the United States, specifically New York. "al final pues ya con veinti ocho años ya muy mayor para ser modelo pues termina su etapa como modelo en parís."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: European Disco Influence
podcast.body: Grace Jones drew extensively from the distinct European version of disco, which differed significantly from the pure, Gloria Gaynor-influenced Afro-American disco that struggled to penetrate Europe. European disco incorporated influences from Germany and a less pronounced focus on black music, and she brought this unique perspective to her music. "Gray Jones no se traía solo esa esa versión tan provocadora tan artística y tan visual de su etapa en en parís sino que se traía muchas influencias de la versión europea que tuvimos a la música disco."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Evolution of Musical Style
podcast.body: Initially a disco artist, Grace Jones evolved her style to incorporate heavy influences from New Wave, the Post Punk scene, funk, technopop, and reggae. This eclectic blend made her music distinct and ahead of its time, particularly for dance clubs in the early 1980s. "Jones started with disco, but then moved toward the style that was heavily influenced by New Wave, the Post Punk scene, funk, techno pop, and reggae."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 4: Alt-Dance

podcast.title: Extensive Use of Narrated Song (1980s)
podcast.body: Grace Jones is noted for extensively using the "canción narrada" (narrated song) technique as a vocal resource throughout the 1980s, especially during her post-disco period. This style is considered a significant precursor to rap, differing primarily from modern rap by its lack of a strict rhythmic structure. "gray Jones en los 80 usó muchísimo la canción narrada es casi la forma de cantar predominante de de gray Jones en su etapa post disco"

srcs.episode: Diferencia entre RAP y HIP-HOP. Por qué ya no son lo mismo.

podcast.title: Fashion Icon Status
podcast.body: Grace Jones was an absolute icon in the fashion industry, working as a model before her musical career. Her background as a model and her status as a fashion icon were crucial to understanding the trajectory of her musical career, illuminating why she became such an important and groundbreaking figure in music. "entendiendo un poco esa parte de la carrera de gresios en la que ella fue modelo y un icono absoluto de la industria de la moda nos ayuda a entender mucho cómo fue acabar a la carrera musical y sobre todo porque fue tan importante y tan reveladora al final."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Humans Album Collaboration
podcast.body: Grace Jones contributed to the Gorillaz album "Humans." "On the record, Dela Soel, Grace Jones, Pusha T, Mavis Staples, those who declined to participate included Morrissey, and Dion Warwick, who had some kind of religion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Gorillaz - A History

podcast.title: Icon of New York Gay & Disco Culture
podcast.body: Grace Jones became an absolute icon within both the New York gay culture and the city's vibrant disco scene, where her provocative style and reinterpretation of the genre resonated strongly. "ella se volvió un absoluto icono dentro de la cultura gaynor y orquina y dentro de la cultura disco te quedó a orquina."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Impact on New York & Visual Iconography
podcast.body: Her arrival in New York led to radical success, as she brought important influences from early 1970s Europe, including her uninhibited and provocative personality and significant artistic perspectives. She understood her potential as a visual icon through her physique and unique stage attire, even if not primarily known for her singing. "Nueva York se echa sus pies porque se trajo influencias muy importantes en la Europa de primeros de los 70."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Influential in 1980s Alternative Circles
podcast.body: Grace Jones was a highly significant figure in alternative music circles during the 1980s, recognized for her distinct dance and reggae-infused style. "Grace Jones was huge in alternative circles in the 1980s for her slinky dance and reggae."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Diversity Show 2021

podcast.title: New York Socialite & Studio 54 Figure (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: Upon her return to New York, Grace Jones quickly established herself within the city's high society, leveraging contacts with photographers from her Paris years. She befriended prominent figures like Andy Warhol and became a regular at Studio 54, known for her provocative and radical personality, which had been shaped by the continuous artistic and fashion provocations prevalent in 1970s Europe. "se hace amiga de gente como Andy Warhol empieza a preguntar el estudio 54 y ya es una persona relativamente conocida en la alta sociedad neoyorkina muy pronto."

podcast.title: Overall Cultural Impact
podcast.body: Grace Jones is celebrated as not just a musical icon, but also an artistic and expression icon, playing an integral role in the history of fashion over the past 50 years. Her pre-music career as one of the most significant models, especially for 1970s haute couture in Paris, and her iconic 1976 Yves Saint Laurent tuxedo runway appearance, were fundamental to her swift and profound impact on disco music. "Realmente ella no es solo un icono musical sino que esto es un icono artístico y un icono de expresión y es parte de la historia de la moda."

srcs.episode: Grace Jones - Inicios de la Disco Queen

podcast.title: Reinterpretation of Disco Music (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: As the initial, Afro-American-influenced phase of disco music began to appear exhausted in the late 1970s, Grace Jones emerged as a pivotal figure in its reinterpretation. She introduced a new approach to disco with more electronic and "discotec" elements, incorporating European disco influences that had not deeply penetrated the American scene. "Gray Jones fue uno de los personajes que ayudaron a la reinterpretación de la música disco porque cuando ya esa etapa tan afroamericana de la música disco estaba votada y parecía que ya no daba más de sí reaparece una nueva manera de ver la música disco con otros tintes más electrónicos y más discotequeros."

podcast.title: Richard Bernstein Collaboration
podcast.body: From the outset of her musical career, Grace Jones collaborated with Richard Bernstein. He was responsible for developing the complete iconography for her album covers and personal styling, crucial elements of her visual identity. "y ya desde un principio ya cuenta con el trabajo de Richard Einstein para trabajar toda la iconografía de sus portadas y su vestimenta y de todo."

podcast.title: Widespread Influence on Artists
podcast.body: Grace Jones exerted a significant influence on a diverse range of artists, including Annie Lennox of Eurythmics, Madonna, Lady Gaga, Rihanna, and Lorde. Her impact extends to the drag queen and cross-dressing scene, solidifying her status as a powerful and transformative figure. "Her influence extends not just to follow her, such as any Linux of the Arithmics, but all the way through Madonna, Lady Gaga, Rihanna, and Lord."
